beats.text: Goliath was not nine feet tall.
beats.scene: Painted giant Philistine warrior in bronze armour silhouetted against a stormy valley sunset. Overlay: crossed-out '2.9 m' counter.

beats.text: Or was he? The manuscripts disagree.
beats.scene: Two ancient scroll fragments side by side in warm lamplight, camera drifting between them. Overlay: split-screen compare, 2.9 m vs 2.0 m.

beats.text: Our standard Hebrew text says six cubits and a span.
beats.scene: Close-up of a scribe's hand copying Hebrew on parchment by oil lamp. Overlay: counter 6.5 cubits.

beats.text: That is about two point nine metres.
beats.scene: Giant warrior silhouette beside a cypress tree at dusk, camera rising. Overlay: scale bar rising to 2.9 m.

beats.text: But the Dead Sea Scrolls say four cubits and a span.
beats.scene: Clay jar and scroll in a Qumran cave lit by a single torch. Overlay: counter 4.5 cubits.

beats.text: Josephus and many Greek manuscripts agree.
beats.scene: Ancient historian writing at a desk, painted in warm candlelight. Overlay: ratio badge 4.5 cubits.

beats.text: That is about two metres. Look at your door.
beats.scene: Warrior standing in a plain wooden doorway, head almost touching the lintel, warm interior light. Overlay: scale bar 2.0 m.

beats.text: Still a giant, when most men stood about one point six metres.
beats.scene: Tall warrior beside average Israelite soldiers in a valley at sunset. Overlay: side-by-side compare 2.0 m vs 1.6 m.

beats.text: His armour weighed five thousand shekels, about fifty-seven kilograms.
beats.scene: Heavy bronze scale armour on a wooden stand, torchlight glinting. Overlay: weight counter 57 kg.

beats.text: The spearhead alone: six hundred shekels, about seven kilograms.
beats.scene: Iron spearhead resting on a rock in low sunlight. Overlay: weight counter 7 kg.

beats.text: Not proven: scribes may have changed the number, and no one knows which is original.
beats.scene: Quill hovering over two different numerals on parchment, soft candlelight. Overlay: question mark between 2.9 m and 2.0 m.

beats.text: So Goliath was not nine feet tall. Two metres, or nearly three?
beats.scene: Giant silhouette at sunset, camera pushing slowly forward. Overlay: choice tags A 2.0 m / B 2.9 m.

youtube.title: How Tall Was Goliath, Really? #shorts
youtube.description:
Goliath is often shown as nearly three metres tall, but the oldest manuscripts disagree. Here is what 1 Samuel 17 and the Dead Sea Scrolls say.
The original height is debated; neither number is proven.
#Goliath #Bible #DeadSeaScrolls #BibleHistory
